I remember hearing that BERT was trained on a large dataset of English text and that it's a bidirectional model, processing the input from both left and right.

Next, the "Attention is All You Need" (AAUN) architecture is another transformer model, but it's more focused on the attention mechanism. I believe the original paper by Vaswani et al. introduced the transformer for machine translation tasks. The encoder in AAUN has 8 layers, each consisting of multiple attention heads.

So, to find the difference, I subtract the number of layers in AAUN from BERT. That would be 12 (BERT) minus 8 (AAUN), which equals 4. Therefore, BERT has 4 more layers than AAUN.
